economy.summary: Big week: the Fed decides on rates Wednesday, Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday, Amazon on Thursday, and Q3 GDP and September PCE inflation come out Thursday morning. Last week, worries about AI spending hit big tech after Meta's report (Oct 22 was the Nasdaq's worst day since June), then Anthropic's IPO filing lifted AI stocks on Monday. The backdrop hasn't changed: a war-driven oil shock is keeping inflation high and the Fed leaning toward hikes while hiring has nearly stopped. That's hard on stocks priced for fast growth and kinder to energy producers, banks and steady defensive companies.
economy.fed: The Fed raised rates in September, its first hike in three years, because oil pushed inflation up. It's expected to hold at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28, but futures see roughly an 80% chance of another hike in December.
economy.fedNext: The Fed announces its decision on Wednesday, Oct 28, at 2 pm ET; this meeting brings no new forecasts. Futures put the chance of no change at about 90% and the chance of a quarter-point hike at the Dec 8–9 meeting at about 80% (CME FedWatch, Oct 26). Thursday's reports on September PCE inflation and Q3 GDP (forecast near 3%) will shape the December decision.
economy.oil: The US–Iran war has largely shut the Strait of Hormuz since late February. Brent crude settled near $117 a barrel on Oct 23, a six-month high, as traders bet the U.S. could resume strikes on Iran; U.S. crude (WTI) was about $101 on Oct 26.

GOOGL: Reports Q3 on Oct 28 after the close. Analysts expect revenue up about 25% to $128B and Google Cloud sales up about 95% to $29.6B (LSEG), while Search growth slows to about 15%; free cash flow is expected to be negative for a second straight quarter because of AI spending. The stock fell 8% from Oct 19 to Oct 26 as AI-spending worries spread after Meta's report. Separately, Anthropic filed for its IPO on Oct 26; Alphabet owns roughly 14% of it, and the filing gives Alphabet an option to buy up to $10B more at the IPO price.
Alphabet and its Anthropic stake (Motley Fool)
MSFT: Reports fiscal Q1 on Oct 28 after the close, a few hours after the Fed decision. Analysts expect revenue up about 17% to $90.7B and Azure cloud growth near 48%, up from 42% (Visible Alpha). Microsoft will report under new segments, "Agents and Infra" and "Devices and Consumer", and disclose Azure's quarterly revenue for the first time.
AMZN: Reports Q3 on Oct 29 after the close. Amazon guided sales to $197B–$202B (up 9–12%) and operating income to $22.5B–$26.5B; analysts expect about $202B in sales, EPS near $1.96 and AWS growth of roughly 35–38%. It raised its 2026 capital spending plan to about $220B, so free cash flow is expected to stay negative. Amazon also owns a large stake in Anthropic (analysts estimate 15–20%), which filed for its IPO on Oct 26.
META: Q3 revenue rose 26% to $64.6B and Q4 is guided to $73B–$76B. But a $9.9B legal charge (a settlement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental-health claims) cut operating income 37%; without it, EPS would have been $7.40 instead of $3.83. Capital spending of $34.9B was more than the business brought in, so free cash flow was negative $2.1B, and Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capex range (now $135B–$145B). It also plans a non-voting Class C share, handed out as a one-for-one stock dividend in January 2027. The stock fell 7% the next day.
Meta sinks as free cash flow turns negative (CNBC)
NVDA: A market-driven week: the stock fell 4.4% on Oct 22 in the AI-spending selloff, then rose 2.4% to $216 on Oct 26 as Anthropic's IPO filing lifted chip stocks; it's about 10% below its record close of $239. Nvidia also expanded its security partnership with CrowdStrike. Next earnings: Nov 18.
HOOD: Reports Q3 on Oct 27 after the close, with a call at 5 pm ET. Analysts expect revenue of about $1.34B–$1.41B and EPS of about $0.50–$0.54, compared with $1.31B and $0.62 in Q2. The stock fell about 4% from Oct 19 to Oct 26 and is down 18% this year.
SOFI: Record Q3: adjusted net revenue rose 44% to $1.37B, adjusted EBITDA rose 70% to $470M, net income was $241M ($0.18 a share, up from $0.11) and members grew 35% to 17.1 million. SoFi raised its 2026 outlook to about $5.04B in adjusted net revenue and $0.61 in EPS, and gave a first 2027 outlook of about $6.4B in revenue and $0.90 in EPS.
UNH: Q3 beat (adjusted EPS $4.69 vs. $4.15 expected) and 2026 guidance was raised to at least $20.50 per share.
TSLA: Q3 revenue was flat at $28.1B, but gross margin improved to 19.6% (from 18.0% a year ago) and adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.45 estimate. GAAP net income fell 43% to $787M, the operating margin was just 2.6%, energy revenue fell 16%, and free cash flow was $1.5B (vs. $4.0B a year ago). Tesla said its robotaxis have driven nearly 2 million unsupervised miles. The stock fell 3% the day after the report, then jumped 5% on Oct 26.
Q3 beat on margins and cash flow (investinglive)
NFLX: Q3 EPS of $0.87 beat the $0.82 estimate and revenue of $12.9B (up 12%) matched, with a 34.6% operating margin. But Q4 revenue guidance of $13.4B came in under the $13.5B expected, and Netflix cut its 2026 ad revenue forecast to about $2.7B from $3B, citing a slower rollout of some ad features. The stock fell 5% the next day and closed at $63.90 on Oct 26, down 32% this year.
Why Netflix fell despite the beat (Finviz)
CRWD: Rose about 15% from Oct 19 to Oct 26 as cybersecurity stocks rallied on worries about a wave of AI-enabled cyberattacks. CrowdStrike also expanded its partnership with Nvidia to build security in at the chip level, and Mizuho raised its price target to $275. The stock has more than doubled this year.
NOW: Rose about 9% from Oct 19 to Oct 26, to its highest level since December, as fears that AI tools would eat into software sales eased. Reports Q3 on Oct 28.
KO: Q3 EPS of $0.91 and revenue of $13.4B beat estimates, and Coca-Cola raised its full-year outlook to about 11% earnings growth. Shares dipped anyway on slowing demand in North America, after a record close on Oct 22; the stock is up about 33% this year.
Coca-Cola pulls back on slowing U.S. demand (Schaeffer's)
BA: Q3 revenue of $24.2B came in slightly above forecasts, but the core loss of $0.34 a share was wider than analysts expected (GAAP loss: $0.26). Free cash flow was positive at $0.5B, the order backlog hit a record $745B, and Boeing delivered 161 commercial jets in the quarter.
PYPL: Q3 adjusted EPS rose 8% to $1.45, well above the roughly $1.31 expected, but revenue grew only 2% to $8.6B, a bit short of forecasts. GAAP EPS fell 4% to $1.25.
NKE: Fiscal Q1 beat on profit (adjusted EPS $0.48 vs. $0.44 expected), but revenue fell 4% to $11.2B, Greater China sales fell 22%, and Nike now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to fall by a high-single-digit percentage with EPS of $1.15 to $1.35 (Wall Street had about $1.67). It also launched a $2.5B cost-savings plan.
JPM: Q3 profit rose 6% to $15.3B and revenue rose 8% to $50.2B, but adjusted EPS of $5.75 missed estimates near $5.85. Equity trading jumped 49%, buybacks were cut 84% from Q2, and the full-year net interest income outlook was raised to about $106B.
TSM: Q3 revenue of $46.7B (up 41%) beat the top of its own guidance; EPS rose 69% with a 58.7% operating margin. TSMC guided Q4 revenue to $52.3B to $54.3B (about 58% growth) and now expects 2026 revenue to grow about 44%.
ASML: Record Q3 sales of 11.7B euros with a 57.5% gross margin. ASML guided Q4 sales to 14.2B to 15.2B euros and full-year 2026 to 44B to 45B euros, saying customers raised equipment plans because of AI.
